name: Keychain across uninstall
plain: On iOS, small secrets stored in the Keychain stay on the device after the app is deleted and come back on reinstall.
meaning: Developers use this to keep an anonymous id or login across reinstalls. It is a durable device level identifier unless the person wipes or restores to a new device.

android.persistence: Keystore keys are deleted at uninstall; Auto Backup can restore app data but not Keystore keys
android.note: Keystore entries are removed with the app

ios.persistence: Survives app deletion; migrates with encrypted backups and device to device transfer; kSecAttrSynchronizable syncs via iCloud Keychain
ios.note: Items persist across uninstall (documented developer behavior, no explicit Apple guarantee); data protection class controls availability

limits.headline: Can keep small secrets on your iPhone that survive after you delete the app
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you delete the app and install it again
can: Store tokens or IDs in the Keychain that stay after you delete the app
Find them again after you reinstall on the same phone
Treat you as a returning user after a reinstall
cannot: Keep them on Android, where deleting the app removes its keystore entries
Count on it as an Apple promise; it is documented developer behavior, not guaranteed
Be available while the phone is locked, if their protection class says so
limits.reach_label: A stable ID that follows reinstalls
limits.differs: iPhone Keychain items usually survive uninstall. Android keystore entries are removed with the app.

story.what_it_is: Small secrets stored in the iPhone keychain can stay after an app is deleted and return on reinstall.
story.for_you: You delete an app and reinstall it, and you are still signed in. You never see why. It feels convenient, but it also means you cannot easily start fresh.
story.for_makers: Makers keep an anonymous ID or login across reinstalls for fraud checks and returning user care. It is a durable device level ID until the phone is wiped.

use_cases.example: A bank app keeps a device ID across reinstalls to spot account takeovers.
A free to play game gives the same trial bonus once, even after you delete and reinstall.
An attribution tool counts a returning device as the same person instead of a new install.
A store keeps you signed in after a reinstall.
A streaming app limits free trials per device, even after you delete the app.
A product team joins sessions before and after a reinstall.
A dating app blocks someone banned from rejoining with the same phone.

story.android_note: Android deletes keystore entries with the app.
story.ios_note: Items stay after uninstall on the same device, and come back with a restored backup.

technical_bounds: Lost on erase or new device unless in encrypted backup
